{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"40071fe4385a80024066c57fe9e985a191a628cbf2cf01a8f2b74f4cf5306d01","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:60","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Downshifting Cautions, Parking, Turn and Hazard Signals, Traffic Mix and Inclement Weather","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Downshifting Cautions, Parking, Turn and Hazard Signals, Traffic Mix and Inclement Weather","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Downshifting Cautions, Parking, Turn and Hazard Signals, Traffic Mix and Inclement Weather

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A05
Partial hydroplaning can begin at thirty-five miles per hour, while complete loss of tire contact can come at fifty-five miles per hour in heavy rain [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint rain; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F30 and sec14-F31.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A06
Low beams are the rule in both fog and heavy rain, while high beams in fog reflect back and blind both you and the oncoming driver [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint visibility; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec14-F37 and sec14-F34.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A03
Hazard flashers warn of a vehicle stopped in a hazardous position and are never used while moving, while turn signals are used for every turn and lane change while moving [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint signals; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec14-F18 and sec14-F24.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A02
Parallel parking starts eighteen inches from the front car and ends with bumpers at least two feet from the neighbors, while the curbside wheels must finish within twelve inches of the curb [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint parking-distances; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F09 and sec14-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
On a hill the front wheels go toward the curb so the car cannot roll free, while the manual also directs turning them to the right uphill or downhill so a loose car rolls away from traffic [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint hill-parking; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F06 and sec14-F07.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A03
Electric signals can fail to cancel or fail to work, while hand signals rarely fail but are hard to see at night, from the right side and through a closed window [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint signals; prereq_hint sec14-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F15 and sec14-F17.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A05
The first drops of rain make the road most slippery because of road oil, while prolonged rain creates the water layer that causes hydroplaning [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint rain; prereq_hint sec14-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F29 and sec14-F30.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A06
Wet brakes are dried by gentle pedal pressure at reduced speed, while a flooded road with fast water over one foot deep is never driven through at all [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint water; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec14-F33 and sec14-F35.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A04
Signaling must begin before you slow for a turn, while the signal itself must run for at least one hundred feet before the turn or lane change [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint signals; prereq_hint sec14-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F21 and sec14-F20.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A01
Downshifting is proper as an emergency measure after brake failure and before a steep downgrade, while downshifting as a routine way to slow is discouraged because following drivers get no stop-lamp warning [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint downshifting; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F04 and sec14-F02.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A05
Larger vehicles are easier to see but harder to operate, while smaller vehicles are more agile but less visible and less protective [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint traffic-mix; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec14-F25 and sec14-F27.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A06
In fog you stop when you cannot see two car lengths, about forty feet, while in heavy rain you stop whenever you cannot see clearly even with the wipers on [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint visibility; prereq_hint sec14-R02; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec14-F37 and sec14-F34.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0076]
